The Stars Never Fade is a digital storybook inspired by NASA's Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge.

The project tells an imaginative story about two real space explorers: Opportunity (Oppy), a Mars rover that operated for almost 15 years, and Eagle, the Apollo 11 Lunar Module that helped carry the first humans to the Moon.

Through an imaginary conversation between Oppy and Eagle, the story explores their journeys, challenges, discoveries, and the legacy they left behind.

Combining real NASA mission information, creative storytelling, and digital illustrations, our project aims to make space exploration more engaging and accessible to young learners.

Our message is simple: Even when a mission ends, its discoveries and contributions are never forgotten.
details:
The Stars Never Fade is a digital storybook created in response to NASA's Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge.

Our project tells an imaginative story about two real space explorers: Opportunity (Oppy), a NASA rover that explored Mars for almost 15 years, and Eagle, the Apollo 11 Lunar Module that helped the first humans land on the Moon.

Through an imaginary conversation between these two explorers, readers discover their missions, challenges, scientific contributions, and lasting legacy. The story is presented in five chapters, combining storytelling, dialogue, and digital illustrations to make space exploration more engaging and easier to understand.

To develop our project, we researched official NASA resources, selected relevant mission facts, and transformed the information into a creative story. We used Canva to write, organize, and design the digital storybook, incorporating NASA images and visual materials. No coding or additional hardware was required.

The creative element of our project is the imaginary conversation between Oppy and Eagle. Although they never actually communicated, their fictional dialogue connects two important moments in space exploration and helps readers understand the value of missions that have ended.

Our project aims to:

  • Raise awareness of the contributions of past space missions.
  • Encourage young learners to explore science and space.
  • Show how scientific information can be shared through creative storytelling.

We considered scientific accuracy, storytelling, visual clarity, and accessibility when developing the project. Real NASA facts are clearly distinguished from the fictional conversation.

Our message is: Even when a mission ends, its discoveries and contributions are never forgotten.
